summary: Bare red-orange fired clay, as in flowerpots, roof and floor tiles.
_comment: Unglazed terracotta: a red-orange earthenware clay fired low and left bare (flower pots, roof and floor tiles, architectural cladding), matte and porous. Opaque: a solid, rough dielectric. Base textures are generated (L2, tools/converters/base/gen_terracotta_unglazed.py; re-made 2026-10-31 for the maintainer's redo, "could pass for painted clay"; it was param-only, L1): the kiln flashes the body in soft clouds 2 to 5 cm across (paler and buff where it ran cooler, deeper red-brown where the flame touched), sparse sand and grog show as pale and dark grains, and the face has open pin pores and a dry, sanded tooth. The mean colour is Physically Based 'Terracotta'. It is the coarser, architectural sibling of Earthenware_Natural (the finer pottery body, anchored to the same entry). Carries every relevant wear layer at 0 (C1): chipped edge wear (overlay 1, damage) and dust as a deposit (Phase10), gated by the Crevice mask (chips in broken patches, dust in the recesses). No third layer is relevant. Not carried: the efflorescence (a pale salt bloom) the wish list also wants, which needs a colour deposit layer. Built by the Phase11 batch.
name: Terracotta_Unglazed_Clean_Base_s01_v01

sources.note: base_color_const is the MEAN of the generated basecolor texture (linear, re-anchored exactly); roughness 1.0 is its ceiling: the map's mean is 0.95, a sanded face keeping a trace of sheen on its grains (judgement).
